title: Kalanj
eyebrow: Anna's people, and the parish nobody has opened
dek: The family this archive's own great-great-grandmother came from — what can be proved about her, what two archives disagreed about, and the parish register that would answer it. The Kalanj genealogy proper is kept in The Blažević Archive; this page is the join, and the evidence on this side of it.
lead: David asked on 29 September 2026 whether Kalanj was a family this site should track and give a page of its own. It was — and building the page found a misreading this archive had carried in fifteen files, and a phrase in the same line of the same entry that no file carried at all. What follows is the evidence on this side of the join, in the order it was read: the baptism, the two things that baptism says which this archive had got wrong or missed, the stone the registers contradict, and eleven photographed graves that suggest a sibling set and cannot yet prove one.
source_kalanj: Ledenice baptismal register, entry 2 of 1864, read from the plate held here at 6×. David's photographs of the Kalanj graves, 29 September 2026. The Blažević Archive's Kalanj page, read 29 September 2026.

sections.h2: It begins with one line in a Vinodol baptism
paras: «Anna, legitima — **Josephus Kalanj et Rosalia nata Perković ejus uxor, Brinjensis Parochiæ ruricolæ**» — at «**Kljenovica N° 22**». Godparents Josephus Ban and his wife Anna; baptised by Vincentius Segulja, parish priest. The register of Ledenice, the Vinodol parish above Crikvenica. (**doc** — the plate is held here and was read at 6×.)

She married **Josip Defranceschi**, the stonecutter's son who brought this archive's line down from Gračišće to the coast, and she is **generation four of [the direct line](/direct-line/)**. Five children are recorded to the couple. Anton Rudolf's baptism is entry 9 of the Ledenice / Klenovica baptismal register for 1890 (born 20 January, baptised 9 February); four further baptismal entries at Crikvenica name the mother **Ana Kalanj**, and those four entries are the reason the next section but two exists.

Two sentences of that one line turned out to be worth a section each. The first is a place name this archive had been reading wrongly since it first transcribed the entry. The second is four words nobody had transcribed at all.

sections.h2: How this household joins the Defranceschi line

sections.lab: Corrected 29 September 2026 · fifteen files, including the pedigree's own wall note
sections.h2: «Rijenovica» does not exist, and the mistake hid a fact
paras: Until today this archive read that place as «**Rijenovica** house 22» and said so in fifteen files. There is no Rijenovica. The word returns **zero hits** in this archive's Croatian gazetteer. The register says **KLJENOVICA** — the older spelling of **Klenovica** — and [the Blažević Archive](https://blazevic.defranceski.com/kalanj/) has read it correctly all along.

What the misreading concealed is the part worth keeping. This site's [Crikvenica page](/crikvenica-house/) already said: «House 22 is somewhere in this line of roofs — **Anton Rudolf Defranceski was born in it on 20 January 1890**.» **Anna was born in the same house twenty-six years earlier.** The archive held «house 22» at both ends of the same family and never joined them, because at one end the village had the wrong name.
The correction is recorded on [corrections](/corrections/), and `check-propagation.py` now holds every file that asserted the old reading.

sections.lab: «Brinjensis Parochiæ ruricolæ» · four words later in the same line
sections.h2: And the same entry says where they came from, which no file of this archive carried
paras: **Country people of the parish of Brinje.** Not one file of this archive carried that phrase, and it is the most important thing in the entry: **the Kalanj were not coastal people.** Brinje is inland, up behind the Velebit gap; they had come down to Klenovica on the shore.

**And the Blažević Archive has since walked through that door.** It called Brinje «the single largest hole in this family» when not one page had been opened. **That is no longer true.** Its own session located the films on 15 September and has been reading the marriage book of 1888–1899 through today, 29 September — and has found **Kalanj men actually resident in the village**: Niko, of Brinje house 231, son of Juro; Mijo, of house 249, born about 1838; and Mate as a witness. Also a **Perković** as a bride, and seven Borić men across four Brinje hamlets. *None of them is yet tied to Anna's household, and this archive does not tie them.* [The family and the findings are kept there.](https://blazevic.defranceski.com/kalanj/)

sections.h2: The oldest open question in this archive is a Kalanj question
paras: The registers name **ANA KALANJ** in all four Crikvenica baptismal entries of her children. The family's own genealogy gives Josip a wife **ANA GRUBIŠIĆ**, 19 September 1863 – 28 May 1936, and that is the name cut on the Crikvenica gravestone.

**The registers govern here and the stone is unexplained.** And the stone no longer exists: the plot was sold to the neighbour of the family house and the monument taken apart, so [the photograph of it](/crikvenica-house/) is now the only record there will ever be.

This is why Anna's page carries **no death date**. The only date on offer belongs to a name this archive cannot yet reconcile with hers, and borrowing it would be the kind of quiet join that the Rijenovica correction above exists to punish. (**open**)

sections.lab: Crikvenica, Novi Vinodolski and Klenovica · photographed 29 September 2026
sections.h2: Eleven stones, and a sibling set taking shape
paras: Eleven Kalanj monuments have been photographed in the three cemeteries and are held here as plates. Which of the three each stone stands in is not distinguished in the photographs and is not guessed.

subs.h3: Four of them cluster around Anna's own generation
paras: **LUKA KALANJ 1859–1944** and **KATA 1860–1942** on a ledger slab; and **ROZALIJA KALANJ 1865–1943**, whose first digit is damaged and was read at 5×. Anna was born in **1864**.

So there are Kalanj born in **1859, 1860, 1864 and 1865** in one small stretch of the Vinodol — and **Rozalija is the name of Anna's own mother**, Rosalia née Perković, which is exactly what a second daughter would be called. A sibling set is the obvious reading: Josip Kalanj and Rosalia's children, with one daughter named for her mother.

subs.h3: It is still a guess, and the test is cheap
paras: **No stone here names a father.** Four birth years in a six-year span, in three small cemeteries of one parish, with a shared given name, is proximity — and this archive has spent the day learning what proximity is worth without a document.

The test is specific and it is the most tractable question on this page: **the Ledenice baptisms of 1855–1870**, where Anna's own entry (number 2 of 1864) already sits, and where her brothers and sisters would sit within a few pages of her. (**open**)

Albert 1895–1945 with five of his household; Petar 1913–1971 and Vera 1917–2011 with the infant Milan 1943–1944; Mate 1928–1992; Franjo 1933–2004; a joint Kalanj–Rebrović stone; Vinko 1901–1961 and Paulina 1904–1984; Josip 1950–1983 with Franjo 1909–1991 and Zora 1923–1999; Tomislav 1935–2006; Judita 1934–2012 with Marijan 1931–2019; and Rozalija's own, with Anton 1897–1977, Marija 1898–1989 and Milan 1927–2006.

subs.h3: One stone carries the šahovnica, and nothing else here does
paras: **OBITELJ KALANJ — MARTIN 1905–1988 and MARTINA 1913–1995.** Two porcelain ovals, a stone cross standing in the gravel above — and propped against the plot, **a pink stone plaque cut with the Croatian chequy shield**.
It is the only national emblem on any stone in this whole set of photographs. It is worth recording as such and **nothing more**: a family put it there, and when or why is not on the stone.

subs.h3: Two photographs could not be stored
paras: They reached this archive inline rather than as files: **that one**, and **LOVRO 1906–1965** with Ana, Ivan and Marijan. They want re-sending if they are to be kept.

sections.lab: Four doors, and what is behind each
sections.h2: What is not known, and is worth asking for

asks.q: Are Luka, Kata and Rozalija Anna's brother and sisters?
asks.a: **Ledenice baptisms, 1855–1870.** Anna's own entry is number 2 of 1864 and has been read. Her siblings would sit within a few pages of it, naming the same father. This is the cheapest question on the page and the one that would turn four stones from proximity into a family.

asks.q: Where is Anna's baptism? — answered: on the wrong side of a line drawn in 1949
asks.a:
**The Blažević Archive is reading the Brinje registers now**, image by image, and has found Kalanj households in the village — houses 231, 249 and 118/189. *That is their work and [it is kept there](https://blazevic.defranceski.com/kalanj/).* **What this archive asked is why none of it reaches Anna, and that now has an answer.**

**A decision of the NRH Ministry of the Interior of 13 May 1949 ordered that every parish register with entries UP TO 1860 be handed to the competent state archive** — while those **from 1860** stayed with the **matični uredi**, the registry offices that needed them for daily work. *(**doc** — Angelika Milić, «Zbirka matičnih knjiga u Hrvatskom državnom arhivu», Arhivski vjesnik 60 (2017), and again in its English abstract.)*

**Anna was born on 3 January 1864. Four years the wrong side of that line.** Her baptism was never going to sit in a state archive's register collection, *because the law that filled those collections stopped at 1860.* **It is not lost. It was left where it was being used.**

**The inventory proves the rule on Brinje's own doorstep.** The collection covers the **Senj-Modruš** diocese — Brinje's own — and its Lika parishes stop exactly where the rule says: **Gospić** runs from 1789 and ends **1858/1859**; **Senj** from 1678 and ends **1858**. *And **Brinje is not in the collection at all** — the word does not appear once in it.*

**So the door is not the film and never was.** *Anna's 1864 entry is with the registry office or the parish at Brinje; Brinje's pre-1860 books are unaccounted for and are either with the **diocesan archive of Gospić-Senj** or did not survive. **Three places to ask, and not one of them is a state archive.*** [The rule, the holdings and the two dead catalogues are in the search log.](/searched/)

asks.q: Who is the Ana Grubišić on the Crikvenica stone?
asks.a: The registers say Josip's wife was Ana Kalanj, four times. The stone said Ana Grubišić, 1863–1936. The stone is destroyed and the photograph is the record. Reconciling the two names is the oldest open question in this archive.
The šahovnica stone (Martin and Martina) and the Lovro 1906–1965 stone arrived inline and could not be stored. They are described here from the images as seen; they are not held.

sections.h2: Where the family itself is kept
paras: The Kalanj genealogy proper — **215 published people, earliest birth 1734**, running through Klenovica and Povile — is kept in [The Blažević Archive](https://blazevic.defranceski.com/kalanj/), and is not rebuilt here. That boundary is right.

It had one cost, and this page is the answer to it: **while each archive read only its own page, the two of them held one baptism and disagreed about the village for months.** What belongs *here* is the join, the evidence photographed on this side, and the disagreements between the two. What belongs *there* is the family.

sections.h2: A Kallayn of the Ledenice parish, thirty-seven years before Anna
paras: **5 November 2026.** Reading the death book of the Vinodol chapter at Bribir (FamilySearch waypoint 9RKB-JWG, image 503, left page, the last entry on it, house margin «N3»), the page gives: «*Die 2da 8bris 1827 mortua est proles dierum 23 ex convulsionibus Nomine Mathea filia Georgii, Dnae Annae* **Kallay…** *ex Parochia Ledenicensi*», buried in the Bribir cemetery. A baby girl, Mathea, 23 days old, daughter of Georgius and of «Domina Anna Kallay…», of the parish of Ledenice. *doc* for the words as far as they go.

**What is not settled.** The surname is cut by the edge of the page: **Kallay** and a last stroke that reads as an *n* (**Kallayn**), and the entry does not say whether it belongs to the mother alone or to both parents. **Kallayn is one of the forms the Record Atlas files as the same family as Kalanj**, so it is a name this archive must count; it is not shown to be Anna's family. The 1864 entry above puts her father Josephus at Klenovica, of the parish of Brinje, and the Ledenice parish is the book it was written in; **nothing here joins a Georgius and an Anna Kallayn of 1827 to him**, and a family of one name in one parish is not one family until a record says so. Kept as a lead for the Ledenice baptisms 1861–94 (waypoint 9R2H-RM4, one year read) and for any Ledenice book before them.

sections.lab: Ledenice births 1861–1894, read page by page · 5 November 2026
sections.h2: Anna's brothers and sisters, on the page, and one godfather in 1894
paras: On 5 November 2026 the whole of the Ledenice baptism volume (FamilySearch waypoint 9R2H-RM4, two books, 1861 to 1894) was looked at once, page by page. The household of **Josip Kalanj and Rosalia Perković of house 22** had been listed on 20 September from the index; this is the same set read on the plates, with three corrections. «**Josephus Kalanj, et Rosalia**» appears as the parents of **Martinus** (born 8, baptised 10 November 1861; entry 59, the mother's cell «Rosalia nata Perković, ruricola»; Klenovica 22), **Anna** (1864, as above), **Lucia** (born 24, baptised 26 May 1866; entry 39), **Franciscus** (born 30 September, baptised 4 October 1868; entry 70, written over 67), **Josephus** (born 5, baptised 7 May 1871; entry 39), **Maria** (born 18, baptised 19 March 1874; entry 28) and **Joannes** (born and baptised 18 July 1877; entry 54, the mother's cell «Rozalia Perković», the first letter of the surname unsettled between P and F; a later note «+ 1877 19/7»: he died the next day). (**doc** for each entry; the left pages of the entries of 1861, 1866, 1868, 1871, 1874 and 1877 were looked at by me, the house cells of those years by a reader's zoom.)

**What the page corrects.** The September table gave Martinus as born on 10 November (that is his baptism; he was born on 8 November) and Maria as born on 19 March (born the 18th). The house is «Klenovica» in 1861, «Ledenice N° 22, in Kljenovice» in 1866, «Kljenovica» in 1868, and «**Povile**» (still N° 22) in 1871, 1874 and 1877: the number never changes, the hamlet's name does. **Only 1861, 1864 and 1877 write the maiden name Perković**; the entries of 1866, 1868, 1871 and 1874 say only «Rosalia ruricola», and that they are one couple rests on the two first names and the house number (**inf**).

**What the page does not show.** No child of the couple is baptised in 1865 (the whole year was read), so the Rozalija of the stone, 1865–1943, is not found here as their daughter: either the stone's year is approximate or she is another Kalanj's child. And a **second Josephus Kalanj**, with **Anna Miletić**, has children at the same house number in 1871, 1874, 1876 and 1881; the Josephus born on 19 September 1871 (not the one of 5 May) carries a later note that a baptismal certificate was issued to him on 24 June 1899 «vjenčanja radi». The identification of the Josip Kalanj who married at Crikvenica in January 1899 rests on his parents as that marriage entry names them, not on either baptismal page.

**Anton Rudolf and Marija Stjepanka again, and a godfather.** Entry 9 of 1890 (image 474, page 124) reads «Anton Rudolf, zakoniti, Josip Defranceschi i žena Ana Kalanj rođena», born **20 January** and baptised **9 February** 1890; the date this archive has often given as his baptism is his birth. Entry 83 of 1892 (image 518, page 166) is «Marija Stjepanka», born 8 and baptised 22 December, with a pencil «u Crkvenici» above the name, the father «Josip Defranceschi klesar». **New:** in entry 59 of 1894 (image 548, right page; Margareta, baptised 23 July 1894, Ivan Komadina and Jela Buneta of «Polje u Mjestu kbroj 39») the godparents' cell reads «**Josip de Franceschi klesar i djevojka Marija Komadina kći pok. Jure**». It is probably Anna's husband, in her own parish in 1894; that is **inf**, and no house is given for him. Nothing else of the name stands in any role in the 559 images, and nothing of Kovačina; the terms and what was not read are in the two rows of 5 November on the [searched page](/searched/).
